post.caption: Collectors smell Bakelite to test it. Chemist Leo Baekeland made Bakelite in 1907. It is often called the first fully synthetic plastic. Once heat sets it, Bakelite stays hard and never melts again. The patent was filed in 1907 and granted in 1909. Makers began using it for costume jewelry in the 1920s. It boomed in the 1930s, when carved bangles were an affordable luxury. Collectors prize rare colors such as cobalt blue. Catalin is Bakelite's cast cousin, known for brighter colors. Hot water or a good rub brings out its chemical smell.
